description: Pages editorial background references, matched only against the primary source attribution. Levels describe documented scholarly influence; they are not inferred from surnames in proof methods or secondary citations.

people.name: Paul Erdős
people.context: Paul Erdős made foundational contributions to number theory and combinatorics and posed many influential problems. This background does not enlarge the particular claim resolved here.

people.name: Kurt Mahler
people.context: Kurt Mahler's work established major methods in Diophantine approximation and transcendental number theory. Credit applies to the exact source question only.

people.name: Alexander Holevo
people.context: Alexander Holevo is a leading contributor to the mathematical foundations of quantum information, including quantum channels and information bounds.

people.name: Richard Stanley
people.context: Richard Stanley's work is foundational in algebraic and enumerative combinatorics.

people.name: Donald Knuth
people.context: Donald Knuth's work on algorithms and their mathematical analysis has foundational influence in computer science and combinatorics.

people.name: Richard Jozsa
people.context: Richard Jozsa made foundational contributions to quantum computation and quantum information, including quantum algorithms and entanglement theory.

people.name: Mary Beth Ruskai
people.context: Mary Beth Ruskai made foundational contributions to quantum entropy inequalities, quantum channels and mathematical quantum information.

people.name: Nilanjana Datta
people.context: Nilanjana Datta is an established quantum information researcher whose work includes information theory and quantum entropies.
